cases.expectation: Per-guild mutation lock prevents overlapping destructive/build mutations; exactly one serialized reconciliation occurs at a time.
Operations targeting the same guild serialize through the shared build lock and persisted state remains internally consistent.
Only one stream becomes configured; duplicate concurrent creation is rejected or reconciled without duplicate managed resources.
Destructive removal and reconstruction cannot interleave in a way that causes unrelated managed resources to be deleted.
Reset participates in the same guild mutation boundary and cannot race with another mutating command.

cases.operation: two role assignments for same member
cases.expectation: Managed role state remains normalized; later state does not contain an accidental impossible combination created by concurrent operations.

cases.operation: two timetable publications for different sections
cases.expectation: Both messages can exist in the one shared timetable channel and their section metadata remains distinguishable.

cases.operation: two exam publications for different sections
cases.expectation: Both exams remain in the shared exam channel with their section identifiers intact.
Previously validated command paths keep their expected behavior after later hardening changes.
Same-name unmanaged resources remain protected and missing/mismatched managed IDs remain fail-closed.
1 and 8 remain valid while 0 and 9 remain rejected.
Authorization model remains owner-or-Administration for management commands and owner-only where specified.
SQLite-backed logical state and JSON recovery do not create duplicate Discord resources on startup.

cases.operation: rename an unmanaged resource to a managed-looking name
cases.expectation: The next managed operation does not silently adopt it when its persisted managed ID is absent.

cases.operation: delete a managed resource externally then rerun build
cases.expectation: Reconciliation detects the missing managed resource and recreates only the intended resource, preserving unrelated IDs.

cases.operation: move a managed channel to another category externally
cases.expectation: Operations that require exact managed identity do not treat the moved channel as the expected resource without explicit reconciliation semantics.
